goals.title: A boatful of friends who won't sit still
goals.critique: This is the boat line again, and this time the rework changes the play, not just the list of errands: the friends become live, wilful loads, so every crossing is an active balancing act and not a static test of a hull. That answers the old worry that one good hull ends the game, and the fish-jump rush that rolls everyone into the bay, with Pinchy still holding the fish, is the best clip on the table. But chaotic passengers in a tippy boat are familiar from party games. 'Call them back across the boat' risks becoming whack-a-mole on scripted moods that the player reacts to rather than reads. Carving, the material half, has shrunk to a prelude, and the road stacks hull buoyancy, moving loads, paddling, live carving and friend minds before the core loop can be played at all.

goals.title: Dam the stream, then let it go
goals.critique: This is round 14's dam again, and the rework fixes its sharpest fault: the burst is now the player's own act, and a flood as big as the dam you built turns building into charging a spring you choose when to release. That gives a loop of build, spend and build bigger with a loud payoff each time. Rigid stones that slide when the push beats friction are an honest, priced substitute for the missing crack model. But damming and flooding are still well worn in sandboxes and god games, so the mechanic people would name the game after belongs to others. The uses of the flood (mill, sand, boat, sandcastles) are a list of targets rather than one deep reason to aim it, and the moment borrows the boat and its passengers from another goal. Sand that the flood carves is a second simulation bet hidden in one road step.
